--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.aggregate_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get aggregate value from total degree of nodes. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.aggregate_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Get aggregate value from total degree of nodes. title: >- [Graph.aggregate_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get aggregate value from total degree of nodes. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get aggregate value from total degree of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L57034-L57176){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.aggregate_degree( agg, conditions=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Aggregate total degree](../assets/graphs/aggregate-degree.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node directed graph with each node's total degree (in plus out) in a badge: A 3, B 3, C 4, D 3, E 1. The card sorts them as 1, 3, 3, 3, 4 and gives the median, 3.0." width="100%"} Computes a single aggregate statistic from the total degree values of all nodes. Works with both directed and undirected graphs. For directed graphs, total degree = indegree + outdegree. Each node's degree is found with `get_degree()` (parallel edges each count, a self-loop counts twice in undirected graphs, and edge weights are ignored), the nodes are optionally filtered with `conditions=`, and the remaining values are reduced to one number. Typical uses: - summarizing how connected a typical node is (`"mean"` or `"median"`) - finding the size of the largest hub (`"max"`) or checking for isolated nodes (`"min"` of `0`) - comparing the connectivity of node groups by running the same aggregation with different `conditions=` Without `conditions=`, `"mean"` gives the same value as `average_degree()`. All nodes in the graph are considered; any node selection is ignored. In directed graphs each degree is counted by scanning the edge list, so the cost grows with nodes times edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [agg]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Aggregation function to apply. Must be one of: - `"sum"`: Sum of all total degrees (twice the number of edges when no `conditions=` are given) - `"min"`: Minimum total degree - `"max"`: Maximum total degree - `"mean"`: Mean total degree - `"median"`: Median total degree (the mean of the two middle values when the number of nodes is even) [conditions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[Callable]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Filter function that takes a node object and returns `True` to include the node in the aggregation. If `None`, all nodes are included. The node object has `id`, `label`, and `attributes` properties; `attributes` is a dictionary, or `None` for a node without attributes, so a safe filter looks like `lambda n: (n.attributes or {}).get("kind") == "gene"`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The computed aggregate total degree value. Returns `0.0` if no nodes match the conditions. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `agg=` is not a valid aggregation function. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~aggregate_in_degree`) : The same summary for in-degree (directed graphs only). [](`~aggregate_out_degree`) : The same summary for out-degree (directed graphs only). [](`~average_degree`) : The mean degree over all nodes. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each edge adds one to the degree of both its ends, so in a random graph with 20 nodes and 35 edges the mean degree is `2 * 35 / 20`, or `3.5`. Unlike the in- and out-degree versions, this works on undirected graphs too: ::: {#8935a83e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_gnm_graph(20, 35, seed=23) graph.aggregate_degree("mean"), graph.aggregate_degree("max") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (3.5, 6.0) ``` ::: ::: ### The club without its leaders The karate club's instructor (member 0) and administrator (member 33) have 16 and 17 friends, the most in the club. On average a member has 4.6, but leaving the two leaders out with `conditions=` brings it down to 3.8: ::: {#29868d46 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate = ec.karate_club() def is_member(n): return n.label not in {"0", "33"} ( karate.aggregate_degree("mean"), karate.aggregate_degree("mean", conditions=is_member), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (4.588235294117647, 3.84375) ``` ::: ::: When the club split, the two factions were about as well connected. The instructor's members have a median of 3.5 friends and the administrator's 3: ::: {#7148ca49 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} { faction: karate.aggregate_degree( "median", conditions=lambda n: n.attributes["faction"] == faction ) for faction in [1, 2] } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1: 3.5, 2: 3.0} ``` ::: ::: Sized by degree, each faction has its leader at the center and a few well-connected members around them: ::: {#0d47d14d .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.plot( color_by="faction", size_by="degree", label_by="label", seed=3 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
